claims.content: The trigger is the User initiating archive creation by selecting one or more objects (files or archives) and invoking an archive-creation command—such as 'Add to archive' via the context menu (right-click), toolbar button, or keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+Alt+A), 'Create archive' from the File menu, or 'Create .zip, new archive'—or by dragging and dropping objects from the computer system into PeaZip.

covered_aspect_ids: trigger event: object selection + command invocation
UI mechanisms: context menu, toolbar, keyboard shortcut

claims.content: The User selects one or more objects (files or archives) and invokes archive creation by pressing the 'Add' button on the toolbar.
The system opens the 'Create .zip, new archive' dialog window.

In the Create archive dialog, the User specifies the output path and filename in the 'Output' field, optionally configures encryption such as a password or keyfile, selects a supported archive format (e.g., 'ZIP') and volume type (e.g., 'Single volume') in the Format options section, and may configure additional options such as appending a timestamp to the archive name or adding each object to a separate archive.
The User reviews the list of objects to be archived in the 'Archiving' section, which displays columns for Name, Type, Size, Folders, Files, Date/time, Attributes, and Full name.
The User confirms the action by clicking the 'Ok' button.

The system performs the archive creation job and displays a progress window (PeaLauncher) that graphically shows the status of the archive creation job, including input/output sizes and compression ratio.

Upon successful completion of the archive creation job, the system displays the confirmation message 'Job successfully completed' along with input size, output size (with compression percentage), and processing time.

Diverges from main flow Step 1: instead of invoking archive creation by pressing the 'Add' toolbar button, the User initiates archive creation by dragging and dropping objects from the computer system into PeaZip; the dragged objects are listed in the archive creation interface as if they had been selected and added with the 'Add' button, allowing the User to fine-tune the operation before confirming or canceling.

Diverges from main flow Step 3: instead of selecting the standard ZIP archive format through the dialog's format controls, the User selects an alternative compression format using keyboard shortcuts—Shift+7 for 7Z, Shift+B for BZip2, Shift+G for GZ, or Shift+T for TAR—before confirming the archive creation.

Diverges from main flow Step 3: the User selects 'Change archive type to 7Z self extracting' via the keyboard shortcut Shift+S to create a self-extracting archive instead of a standard archive format.

Diverges from main flow Step 3: in the Format options section, the User optionally selects 'Add each object to a separate archive' to create multiple archives rather than the default single-archive output.
Diverges from main flow Step 3: in the Format options section, the User optionally selects 'Append timestamp to archive name' to produce an archive name variant instead of the default archive name.

Diverges from main flow Step 3: in the Format options section, the User optionally enables 'TAR before' to create a TAR-wrapped archive within ZIP format instead of the default single-volume ZIP creation.
At main flow step 3, if the User attempts to create an archive in a read-only supported format, the system prevents the creation because compression to these formats is not possible.

At main flow step 6, if an error occurs during execution of the archive creation job, the PeaLauncher progress/execution window is kept open as part of its configuration to 'Keep open only if needed (errors, list, test...)' to allow the User direct inspectional knowledge of the results.

At main flow step 6, if issues arise during archive creation, the PeaLauncher progress window includes a Console tab that provides access to console output, including detailed error logs or command-line output, for diagnosing the issues.

claims.content: A new compressed archive file has been created in the selected storage space with the specified name, format (e.g., ZIP), and configured options, including encryption with the specified password and optional keyfile when configured.

Provided the User did not configure the 'Add each object to a separate archive' option, the created archive contains the content of the selected objects within a single compressed unit, enabling multiple objects to be handled and managed as one entity.
If the User configured split volumes, the successful output consists of multiple archive files whose individual sizes are defined by the User.

The system displays a confirmation window with the message 'Job successfully completed', along with input size, output size (with compression percentage), processing time, and 'Explore' or 'Ok' buttons.
The system provides a configuration option to 'Open output path when job completes', allowing the User to view the destination folder after the archive creation finishes.

inconsistency_hints: Main flow step 3 allows the user to configure 'adding each object to a separate archive', which produces multiple independent archives. Postcondition 2 unconditionally states the created archive contains the selected objects within a single compressed unit, so the main flow can lead to a state where this postcondition does not hold.

Main flow does not include configuring the 'Open output path when job completes' option or describe the system opening the destination folder after success. The postcondition claims this automatic behavior, but the main flow provides no path to it and the cited evidence only confirms the option exists, not that it triggers the opening.
